transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

My mind keeps getting stuck on the same upsetting thoughts about messing things up for my family and at work, and I can’t let them go. It’s just incredibly exhausting, and I feel like I'm constantly trapped in my own head.
When these thoughts come up, do they feel intrusive and unwanted, and do you do anything repetitive to try to neutralize them or reduce your anxiety, like checking, counting, or seeking reassurance?

Yes, they are completely unwanted and feel impossible to stop, like my brain is constantly replaying worst-case scenarios. To cope with the anxiety, I end up rereading emails, medical notes, and server configs three or four times, or silently running through mental checklists until it feels "just right."
Do these thoughts and checking rituals take up more than an hour a day, or significantly interfere with your work, home life, or relationships?

Yes, they easily take up hours every day, especially when I'm lying awake at night caught in those loops or wasting time constantly rereading emails and medical notes. It has seriously interfered with my life; I've started missing details at work and had to pull back from community events and mentoring because I'm just too mentally drained. Even my friends have noticed that I'm too trapped in my head to enjoy hiking anymore.
Do you recognize these thoughts and checking behaviors as coming from your own mind and as excessive or unreasonable, even though they feel hard to control?

Yes, absolutely—I know these thoughts are coming from my own mind and that they are completely irrational and excessive. Even though I know I'm wasting time and that the worries are unreasonable, I still feel this overwhelming, uncontrollable urge to do the double-checking anyway.

When you feel the urge to reread or check, do you ever believe that something truly terrible will happen unless you do it, or do you mainly recognize the fear as unreasonable but still feel unable to stop?

I mainly recognize that the fear is unreasonable, but I still feel completely powerless to stop the urge to check. Even though I know it's irrational and that I'm wasting time, I get trapped by the "what ifs" and just can't move on until it feels "just right."
Do you also have any repetitive behaviors or mental rituals besides checking, such as washing, ordering, counting, repeating words, or arranging things until they feel "just right"?

Yes, besides the physical checking, I silently run through mental checklists and repeat specific phrases in my head. I get completely stuck and feel like I can't move on to the next task until everything feels "just right." It's a mental routine I feel forced to complete before I can do anything else.
